name: Chinese unification
summary: Chinese unification, as Beijing advances it, holds that Taiwan is an inseparable part of China and that the divided state left by the civil war must be reunified, preferably peacefully under one country, two systems, but with force reserved against secession or foreign interference. It ties unification to national rejuvenation and treats the question as purely internal. It is a single-issue territorial doctrine, so it says little on economic, social or cultural questions.
scope: The People's Republic of China's official unification doctrine from Deng Xiaoping's one country, two systems through the 2005 Anti-Secession Law and the 2022 white paper under Xi Jinping. It excludes the Republic of China/KMT version, in which unification would occur under the ROC, and pro-unification currents in Taiwan that differ from Beijing's formula. Statements outside the Taiwan question are mostly inferred from general PRC state doctrine and marked low confidence.

universal-healthcare.rationale: Unification doctrine is silent on health policy; the white paper promises equal treatment for Taiwan residents, and PRC state doctrine favours state-provided welfare, so mild agreement is inferred.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: The unification program says nothing on wages and Beijing's line is mixed, so adherents have no stated position here.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: Official PRC doctrine keeps a state-led economy with markets under party direction; one-country-two-systems preserves Taiwan's capitalism but does not claim markets beat governments.

public-ownership.rationale: Mainland doctrine keeps public ownership dominant while promising Taiwan its own economic system, so unification adherents are split or indifferent on the question.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: Nothing in unification doctrine bears on taxation of the wealthy; one-country-two-systems explicitly leaves Taiwan's fiscal system alone.

unions-good.rationale: Not addressed; PRC doctrine favours state-sanctioned unions only, and the unification program is silent.

property-fundamental.rationale: The white paper pledges to protect private property in Taiwan after unification, but the mainland system does not treat property as a near-inviolable right, so no firm stance.

regulate-corporations.rationale: Not addressed by the unification program; no clear adherent position is documented.

cut-welfare.rationale: Inferred from PRC state doctrine, which treats welfare as a state responsibility rather than a dependency problem; unification texts are silent.

worker-ownership.rationale: Mainland doctrine favours state and mixed ownership rather than worker-owned firms, and the unification program does not endorse worker ownership.

surveillance-ok.rationale: Inferred from the state's security-first posture (the Anti-Secession Law prioritises countering separatism); unification texts do not address surveillance directly.

legalize-drugs.rationale: Not addressed; PRC state policy is strict prohibition, which is the inferred position.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: The white paper attacks separatist propaganda and "de-sinicization", but this is not a hate-speech doctrine, so no clear stance.

strong-leader.rationale: Deng's framework has Beijing intervening when needed and the party centralised under a paramount leader; inferred, not a unification tenet.

state-harmful.rationale: Unification is a state-building project: the law makes reunification a state duty and authorises the State Council and military to enforce it.

limit-guns.rationale: Not addressed in unification texts; PRC state policy bans civilian gun ownership, so mild agreement inferred.

empower-police-military.rationale: Article 8 authorises military force as a last resort and the white paper refuses to renounce it, implying support for strong armed forces.

legalize-sex-work.rationale: Not addressed; PRC law prohibits sex work, which is the inferred state position.

decide-locally.rationale: Unification rests on a single sovereign centre; Taiwan would be a special administrative region with autonomy only as granted under one China.

rehabilitation.rationale: Not addressed by unification doctrine; no basis for a position.

traditional-family.rationale: The white paper stresses shared Chinese culture and heritage across the Strait, from which mild support for traditional values is inferred.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: Unification doctrine is silent, and Taiwan's legal same-sex marriage is not cited as an obstacle; adherents are indifferent.

abortion-legal.rationale: Not addressed by the unification program.

more-religion-public.rationale: The white paper promises freedom of religious belief in Taiwan but mainland doctrine keeps religion under state supervision; inferred mild disagreement.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: Not addressed; unification doctrine has no racial-justice program.

gender-social-construct.rationale: Not addressed by the unification program.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: The white paper frames shared Chinese identity and culture as the basis of unification and opposes "de-sinicization" in Taiwan.

gradual-change.rationale: Unification is pursued in "steps and phases" but the aim is radical change in the Strait's status, so this general claim does not map cleanly.

reduce-immigration.rationale: Not addressed by the unification program.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: The white paper rejects external interference and treats the Taiwan question as purely internal, opposing UN or foreign roles in it.

free-trade.rationale: The white paper promotes cross-Strait economic integration and a common market, but state doctrine is not a general free-trade creed.

nation-first.rationale: The white paper subordinates cross-strait and international considerations to sovereignty, territorial integrity and national rejuvenation.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: Article 3 and the white paper insist the Taiwan question is purely internal with no outside interference, a principle of non-intervention.

open-borders.rationale: Inferred from the emphasis on sovereignty and territorial borders; unification doctrine treats borders as defining state integrity.

limit-growth.rationale: National rejuvenation is tied to development and growth; unification texts do not address environmental limits.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: Not addressed by the unification program.

tech-solves-problems.rationale: Not addressed by the unification program.

expand-nuclear.rationale: Not addressed by the unification program.

revolution-justified.rationale: The CCP was founded by revolution but the law targets secession as unlawful and states the PRC's legitimacy as settled; inferred mild disagreement for present-day politics.

experts-over-public.rationale: Not addressed; no clear adherent position.

central-planning.rationale: Mainland doctrine now favours a socialist market economy; the unification program does not address planning.

socialized-markets.rationale: Not addressed; the unification program preserves Taiwan's own economic system.

land-value-tax.rationale: Not addressed by the unification program.

tax-inheritance.rationale: Not addressed by the unification program.

basic-income.rationale: Not addressed by the unification program.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: Not addressed; the white paper offers economic integration and favourable trade for Taiwan rather than a tariff doctrine.

state-directs-investment.rationale: Inferred from PRC state-led development practice; the white paper proposes state-backed integration projects such as a Fujian pilot zone.

widespread-small-property.rationale: The white paper promises protection of Taiwan's private property, but takes no stance on property distribution.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: Official doctrine is a socialist market economy; abolition of money is a distant aim not pursued in the unification program.

abolish-central-banks.rationale: Inferred from state-led economic doctrine; unification texts do not address central banking.

corporatist-bargaining.rationale: Not addressed by the unification program.

one-party-rule.rationale: The unification program is a CCP policy and Beijing's one-country-two-systems rests on party-led central authority, though the Taiwan question itself does not require this answer.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: Inferred from republican state doctrine; not addressed in unification texts.

democracy-best.rationale: Beijing claims its system is a "whole-process democracy" but Deng held Western-style systems unsuitable; adherents give no clear endorsement.

direct-votes.rationale: Beijing's approach to Taiwan rests on negotiation among authorities, not referendums, and rejects plebiscites on status; inferred.

workers-councils.rationale: Not part of the unification program; state doctrine rests on party-led institutions.

right-to-secede.rationale: Article 2 states secession will not be allowed under any name or by any means, and Article 8 authorises force against it.

natural-rulers.rationale: Not addressed in the sources read; no adherent position is documented.

political-violence-never.rationale: Article 8 and the white paper explicitly keep the option of force against secession, so violence is not ruled out.

war-builds-character.rationale: Beijing presents force as a last resort and Article 9 stresses minimizing losses, so it does not celebrate war.

separate-church-state.rationale: Not addressed by the unification program.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: Inferred from secular state doctrine; unification texts are silent on scripture.

private-courts-defense.rationale: The state alone holds the military decision under Article 8 (State Council and Central Military Commission), so private defence is rejected.

military-superiority.rationale: Credible force against Taiwan independence is the backstop of the policy in Article 8 and the white paper, implying military strength relative to rivals.

ethnic-nation.rationale: The white paper frames the Chinese nation as a shared kinship and heritage across the Strait, though the PRC officially recognises many ethnic groups.

class-struggle-history.rationale: Unification doctrine frames history as national division and rejuvenation, not class conflict.

equal-outcomes.rationale: Not addressed by the unification program.

indigenous-land-authority.rationale: The white paper treats Taiwan as a unitary part of China; autonomy is state-granted, not by indigenous rights. Inferred.

colonial-reparations.rationale: The white paper cites Japanese colonial rule and Taiwan's cession but takes no clear stance on reparations.

civilizational-union.rationale: Beijing grounds unification in shared Chinese civilisation and history spanning both sides of the Strait; the statement is general but fits that logic.

self-interest-moral.rationale: Collective national interest is prioritised in state doctrine; inferred from the framing of reunification as a shared duty of all Chinese (Article 4).

duties-before-rights.rationale: Article 4 frames reunification as a sacred duty of all Chinese people, including Taiwan compatriots, placing national obligation first.

nature-intrinsic-value.rationale: Not addressed in the sources read; no adherent position is documented.

limit-population.rationale: Not addressed by the unification program.

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: Inferred from national-rejuvenation framing, which treats modernisation as positive.

accelerate-technology.rationale: Not addressed by the unification program.

human-enhancement.rationale: Not addressed in the sources read; no adherent position is documented.

algorithmic-government.rationale: Not addressed in the sources read; no adherent position is documented.

unbreakable-encryption.rationale: Inferred from state security doctrine; unification texts silent.

restore-past-order.rationale: Rejuvenation is both restoring historical unity and forward progress, so adherents see no tradeoff to choose between.

results-over-ideology.rationale: Not addressed; Deng's pragmatism favours results, but the unification line is framed as principle.

direct-action.rationale: The law channels change through state authority and negotiation (Article 7), not direct action.

means-match-ends.rationale: Not addressed in the sources read; no adherent position is documented.

return-to-foraging.rationale: Inferred from national rejuvenation and development goals; unification texts are silent.

abolish-division-of-labor.rationale: Not part of the unification program.

distribute-by-need.rationale: Not addressed in the sources read; no adherent position is documented.

production-for-use.rationale: Not addressed in the sources read; no adherent position is documented.

profit-exploitation.rationale: The white paper promises Taiwan capitalism would be preserved after unification, which contradicts treating profit as exploitation.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: Not addressed; unification texts do not invoke it.

collective-farming.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from the mainland's post-collective rural reforms.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: Not addressed; the white paper blames outside powers' interference, not capitalism as such.

taxation-theft.rationale: Inferred from state doctrine; not addressed in unification texts.

harm-principle.rationale: Not addressed in the sources read; no adherent position is documented.

individual-rights-only.rationale: Article 4 frames duty to nation and Article 6 protects residents' rights, but national interest takes priority over individual claims. Inferred.

conscription.rationale: Inferred from the state's mobilisation under Article 8 and the PRC's conscription law; unification texts do not address it.

exit-over-voice.rationale: Not part of unification doctrine; Beijing's approach insists on binding, not exit-based, sovereignty.

positive-liberty.rationale: Not addressed in the sources read; no adherent position is documented.

media-academia-power.rationale: The white paper blames separatist propaganda for identity problems but does not make a claim about media power generally.

hereditarian-race.rationale: Not addressed; official line is ethnic unity among Chinese, not a race-science doctrine.

organic-representation.rationale: Not addressed in the sources read; no adherent position is documented.

total-state.rationale: Not addressed; one-country-two-systems explicitly allows distinct systems, which cuts against a total-state reading.

national-rebirth.rationale: The white paper says reunification is essential to the great rejuvenation of the Chinese nation, the central justification.

territorial-expansion.rationale: Beijing frames Taiwan as recovering existing territory, not expansion, so adherents would reject the label but support retaking.

no-neutral-knowledge.rationale: Not addressed in the sources read; no adherent position is documented.

universal-morality.rationale: Not addressed in the sources read; no adherent position is documented.

single-common-good.rationale: The white paper frames unification as in the common interest of all Chinese people, a single national good.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: Not addressed in the sources read; no adherent position is documented.

diaspora-return-right.rationale: Not addressed beyond the white paper's calls for Taiwan compatriots to share in the nation.

revive-national-language.rationale: Not addressed in the sources read; no adherent position is documented.

workplace-democracy.rationale: Not addressed in the sources read; no adherent position is documented.

school-vouchers.rationale: Not addressed in the sources read; no adherent position is documented.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: Not addressed in the sources read; no adherent position is documented.

economic-freedom.rationale: Deng argued political systems need not match economic systems; inferred rejection of the claim that political freedom needs economic freedom.

rule-by-example.rationale: Not addressed in the sources read; no adherent position is documented.

national-self-determination.rationale: The white paper claims the Chinese nation's right to a unified state while denying Taiwan's separate self-determination, so the general principle is read as applying to the whole Chinese nation.

force-without-un.rationale: Article 8 authorises force on Beijing's own decision, and the white paper rejects outside authority over the Taiwan question.

reason-over-faith.rationale: Not addressed in the sources read; no adherent position is documented.

welfare-for-citizens.rationale: Not addressed in the sources read; no adherent position is documented.

work-for-welfare.rationale: Not addressed in the sources read; no adherent position is documented.

class-collaboration.rationale: Official doctrine stresses social harmony; inferred, not a unification tenet.

sacrifice-heritage.rationale: The white paper opposes de-sinicization and treats shared cultural heritage as the basis of unity.

dominated-front.rationale: The white paper accuses the US of using Taiwan to contain China and calls on others to oppose hegemonism; a common front is inferred.

workers-nation.rationale: Not addressed in the sources read; no adherent position is documented.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: Not addressed in the sources read; no adherent position is documented.

ban-interest.rationale: Inferred from market-based financial system on both sides; not addressed.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: Unification doctrine asserts one Chinese nation and equal treatment of Taiwan residents, incompatible with legal racial separation.

state-class-instrument.rationale: Not addressed in the sources read; no adherent position is documented.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: Not addressed in the sources read; no adherent position is documented.

assimilate-immigrants.rationale: Not addressed in the sources read; no adherent position is documented.

proportional-representation.rationale: Not addressed in the sources read; no adherent position is documented.

national-mission.rationale: The white paper rejects exporting a system and says Taiwan keeps its own; it asks for no spread of the mainland model abroad.

patriarchy-structural.rationale: Not addressed in the sources read; no adherent position is documented.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: The white paper attacks Taiwan's pro-independence authorities, but does not denounce political elites generally.

heritable-defect-limits.rationale: Not addressed; inferred disagreement from official stance.

security-forces-accountable.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from state doctrine that does not accept external accountability for security forces.

night-watchman-state.rationale: The Anti-Secession Law gives the state wide duties of economic, cultural and security integration (Articles 5, 6), not a minimal role.

discourage-race-mixing.rationale: Unification doctrine seeks closer ties and integration among all Chinese, rejecting this.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: The white paper promises equal treatment of Taiwan compatriots, but the statement is general; mild agreement inferred.

socialism-one-country.rationale: Official doctrine is socialism with Chinese characteristics in one country; the unification program does not invoke world revolution.

settler-state-colonial.rationale: Not addressed beyond the white paper's account of Taiwan's colonial past.

uniform-civil-code.rationale: One-country-two-systems preserves separate legal systems for Hong Kong, Macau and a unified Taiwan, a form of legal pluralism by region.

restrict-conversion.rationale: Not addressed in the sources read; no adherent position is documented.

no-religion-state-schools.rationale: Not addressed in the sources read; no adherent position is documented.

state-strengthens-encirclement.rationale: The white paper stresses a strong state and countering hostile external forces, but it is not framed in Marxist terms; inferred mild agreement.

consent-of-governed.rationale: Beijing rejects a Taiwanese vote on status: the white paper treats unification as a national matter, though it promises consultation.

trade-surplus.rationale: Not addressed in the sources read; no adherent position is documented.

population-transfer.rationale: Article 9 commits to protecting Taiwan civilians and residents, which excludes forced removal.

initiating-force-wrong.rationale: Article 8 authorises the state to initiate force under stated conditions and the white paper refuses to renounce it.

competition-drives-progress.rationale: Not addressed in the sources read; no adherent position is documented.

ban-extremist-parties.rationale: The law bars secession "under any name or by any means" and Beijing bans pro-independence politics at home; it supports outlawing such parties.

freedom-as-non-domination.rationale: Not addressed in the sources read; no adherent position is documented.

separated-powers.rationale: Official doctrine rejects Western separation of powers; unification texts do not address it, so inferred.

vanguard-party.rationale: CCP doctrine; the unification program is a party policy but does not itself restate vanguardism.

priority-to-poor.rationale: Not addressed in the sources read; no adherent position is documented.

right-to-buy-council-homes.rationale: Not addressed in the sources read; no adherent position is documented.

restrict-strikes-picketing.rationale: Not addressed in the sources read; no adherent position is documented.

population-causes-poverty.rationale: Not addressed in the sources read; no adherent position is documented.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: Not addressed in the sources read; no adherent position is documented.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: Article 8 authorises extraordinary measures in a secession crisis, so emergency powers are inferred to be acceptable.

price-controls-essentials.rationale: Not addressed in the sources read; no adherent position is documented.

party-controls-media.rationale: CCP media control is documented practice; unification texts attack separatist propaganda but do not discuss media control itself.

party-commands-army.rationale: The Central Military Commission, a party body, decides on force in Article 8, reflecting party command of the army.

long-naturalization-wait.rationale: Not addressed in the sources read; no adherent position is documented.

representatives-worker-pay.rationale: Not addressed in the sources read; no adherent position is documented.

party-discipline-binding.rationale: CCP democratic centralism; not specific to the unification program.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: The white paper says sovereignty is indivisible and rejects any "two Chinas" or EU-style arrangement; Beijing rejected such proposals.

head-commands-forces.rationale: Not addressed in the sources read; no adherent position is documented.

church-by-bishops.rationale: Not addressed in the sources read; no adherent position is documented.

defeat-own-government-war.rationale: Inferred from nationalist doctrine of national unity in conflict.

censor-art-for-virtue.rationale: Not addressed in the sources read; no adherent position is documented.

unlimited-reelection.rationale: Not addressed by the unification program.

recall-officials.rationale: Not addressed in the sources read; no adherent position is documented.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: The white paper opposes foreign military involvement around Taiwan, but it is about US alliances rather than a general policy; inferred.

abolish-rental-housing.rationale: Not addressed in the sources read; no adherent position is documented.

people-in-arms.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from professional-army doctrine.

rural-life-healthier.rationale: Not addressed in the sources read; no adherent position is documented.

reunify-divided-nation.rationale: The central aim: the white paper and Article 4 call national reunification the duty of all Chinese, treating the 1949 division as a civil-war remnant.

educated-out-of-touch.rationale: Not addressed in the sources read; no adherent position is documented.

cultures-equal-different.rationale: Not addressed in the sources read; no adherent position is documented.

death-penalty.rationale: PRC retains capital punishment, but the unification program does not address it.

sex-ed-in-schools.rationale: Not addressed in the sources read; no adherent position is documented.

creationism-in-schools.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from secular state education.

restrict-pornography.rationale: PRC bans pornography; unification texts silent.

citizenship-by-descent.rationale: The white paper treats Taiwan residents as Chinese compatriots by descent and nation, so descent-based membership is inferred.

minority-language-support.rationale: Not addressed in the sources read; no adherent position is documented.

religious-exemptions.rationale: Not addressed in the sources read; no adherent position is documented.

encourage-eccentricity.rationale: Not addressed in the sources read; no adherent position is documented.

sovereign-debt-cancellation.rationale: Not addressed in the sources read; no adherent position is documented.

independence-needs-economic-change.rationale: Not addressed in the sources read; no adherent position is documented.

constituent-assembly.rationale: Unification is negotiated between authorities under one China, not through a new constituent assembly.

restrict-freedoms-for-growth.rationale: Deng argued that stability precedes development and Western-style political systems are unsuitable; inferred from Deng's framing in one-country-two-systems.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: Not addressed in the sources read; no adherent position is documented.

independent-nuclear-deterrent.rationale: PRC maintains its own deterrent; unification texts do not address it.

direct-election-head-of-state.rationale: Not addressed; PRC head of state is chosen by the legislature.

central-bank-independence.rationale: Not addressed; PRC central bank is under the State Council.

no-land-for-peace.rationale: Territorial integrity is non-negotiable in Article 2; Beijing treats Taiwan as national territory that it will not give up.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: Inferred from socialist doctrine; not addressed in unification texts.

soviet-state-capitalist.rationale: Not addressed; official PRC line treats the Soviet period as socialist.

precautionary-principle.rationale: Not addressed in the sources read; no adherent position is documented.

collective-defense.rationale: The white paper opposes foreign military alliances and US defence commitments toward Taiwan as interference.

annexed-territory-occupation.rationale: Beijing denies Taiwan is annexed territory, and calls Hong Kong and Taiwan matters internal; inferred disagreement.

force-to-prevent-secession.rationale: Article 8 authorises non-peaceful means if secession occurs or peaceful reunification is exhausted, and the white paper refuses to renounce force.

region-keeps-system.rationale: One country, two systems is the core offer, with Article 5 allowing Taiwan to keep different systems and a high degree of autonomy.

missingStatements.text: A country may use military force to prevent a region from separating from it.
missingStatements.rationale: Article 8 authorises non-peaceful means if secession occurs or peaceful reunification is exhausted, and the white paper refuses to renounce force.

missingStatements.text: A region could join a larger state while keeping its own economic and legal system and a high degree of autonomy.
missingStatements.rationale: One country, two systems is the core offer, with Article 5 allowing Taiwan to keep different systems and a high degree of autonomy.

missingStatements.text: Whether a region belongs to a country should be settled by the country as a whole, not by a vote of that region alone.
missingStatements.rationale: The white paper and Article 3 call the Taiwan question an internal matter for all Chinese people, which excludes a Taiwanese-only decision.

missingStatements.text: Foreign governments should not interfere in the dispute over a territory's status.
missingStatements.rationale: Article 3 and the white paper say no outside interference will be tolerated in resolving the Taiwan question.
missingStatements.declined: Specific to the Taiwan dispute; foreign non-interference is not a defining position beyond it and is covered loosely by end-foreign-alliances and dominated-front.

notes: Taiwanese pro-unification strands, especially within the KMT, would answer differently: they favour the ROC framework and reject one country, two systems. Most Taiwanese polls show little support for unification. Unification is a single-issue doctrine, so many answers are inferred from wider PRC state doctrine.
